News.title: ‘It’s not if, it’s when’, first Labour MP calls on Keir Starmer to resign over ‘absolute mess’ of Mandelson vetting
News.content:
A LABOUR MP has broken ranks to call for Sir Keir Starmer to resign amid the Downing Street “psychodrama”.

Backbencher Jonathan Brash insisted the Lord Mandelson affair has led him to call for the Prime Minister to quit saying it’s not “if, but when” he leaves.



His intervention comes as Number 10 have been unable to shake off the controversy around the ex-Labour grandee’s appointment to the UK ambassador job.

Two other Labour MPs Clive Lewis and Peter Lamb have also called on him to walk away from office.



When asked why Sir Keir should resign: “Why? Because ultimately, we’ve become completely consumed by this turmoil at a time when that is not what the British public are focused on.

“They are focused on their cost of living. They are focused on the NHS. It’s a reasonable thing to set a timetable to get this done in an orderly way, because we have got a very, very big job ahead of us.”

Brash also told GB News that nobody “reasonably expects” Sir Keir to lead Labour into the next election. Sir Keir became Labour leader in 2020 and led the party to a massive majority in 2024.

It comes after his premiership has become engulfed by the Mandelson scandal and a series of damaging policy u-turns.

Mr Brash, who represents Hartlepool, added: “I’ve got to be clear, I am completely fed up to the back teeth of this psychodrama in Westminster, the own goals that are coming from the heart of this government.

“Meanwhile, we’ve got fantastic Labour councillors, canvassers, activists up and down the country, working hard and delivering for their constituencies, like mine in Hartlepool, facing local elections in the shadow of this absolute mess. They just need to get a grip.

“I’m completely fed up about it, and I think it’s got to the point now where I genuinely think that, as far as the Prime Minister is concerned, it’s not a case of if, it’s when.

“I just think we need to get a handle on this, because people out there are worried about their cost of living, they’re worried about their NHS, they’re worried about crime on their streets, and we’re completely consumed by this scandal, and it’s completely unacceptable.



“And I’m sure you can tell, I’m quite angry about it.

“Ultimately, we’re in a situation now where I don’t think anyone reasonably expects the Prime Minister to lead the party into the next election.

“I think that we have to refocus this government on the priorities of the British people, refocus it on delivering, which fantastic candidates and councils are doing up and down the country right now in constituencies like Hartlepool, where they’re bringing investment.”

“You heard from the Prime Minister himself in there, where he said that, nothing will distract him from delivering from our country.

“I mean, you know what this government is doing to deliver for working people, from tackling the cost of living, cutting NHS waiting lists, to investing in local communities to restore pride.



When asked if the PM going to resign before next election, the spokesman replied: “No.”

Meanwhile, Sir Keir ex-chief of staff Morgan McSweeney has been summoned to appear before the Foreign Affairs Committee of MPs next Tuesday amid the Peter Mandelson vetting scandal.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mr McSweeney, widely regarded as a protege of Lord Mandelson, resigned in February over his part in the peer’s appointment to the Washington DC posting.

News.title: ‘Will he finally take responsibility & go?’, Badenoch slams Starmer over Mandelson vetting & Labour ‘old boys’ club’
News.content:
ON ANOTHER PLANET ‘Will he finally take responsibility & go?’, Badenoch slams Starmer over Mandelson vetting & Labour ‘old boys’ club’

KEMI Badenoch launched a blistering attack on Sir Keir Starmer today fuming: “I don’t know what planet the Prime Minister is on.”

She accused him of running an “old boys club” after more allegations surrounding the Mandelson scandal came to light.





And she repeated her call for Sir Keir to stand down, blasting: “Will the Prime Minister finally take responsibility and go?”

Sir Keir’s premiership was thrown into fresh crisis this week over his decision to appoint Lord Mandelson as US ambassador despite his links to paedophile financier Jeffrey Epstein and foreign businesses.

Tory leader Ms Badenoch told PMQs that handing Lord Peter Mandelson the plum job was a “national security risk”.

She told the Commons: “I don’t know what planet the Prime Minister is on, appointing someone with known links to the Kremlin is not full due process.

“If anybody had brought that sort of name to me when I was a secretary of state, I would have said ‘no way’.”

It comes after bombshell evidence was dunked on the PM by former Foreign Office boss Sir Olly Robbins yesterday.

The ex-mandarin – sacked by the PM last week – told of “constant pressure” from No10 to approve Lord Mandelson’s security vetting.

Sir Olly said No10 had taken a “dismissive approach” to the Labour peer’s security vetting.



And the PM’s team put “constant pressure” on him to rush through Lord Mandelson’s appointment as US ambassador — and gave him classified documents before getting clearance.

Pressure on the PM will continue next week when his former chief of staff Morgan McSweeney is set to appear before the Foreign Affairs Committee.

SHOW TIME By SOPHIA SLEIGH Sir Keir Starmer’s former powerful chief of staff will have his say next week on the Mandelson scandal engulfing the Government. Morgan McSweeney has been summoned to appear before the Foreign Affairs Committee of MPs on Tuesday. Mr McSweeney, seen as a protege of Lord Mandelson, resigned in February over his part in the peer’s appointment to the Washington posting. He will follow an appearance showing on Thursday by Cat Little, the most senior Cabinet Office civil servant. Last week she revealed to the PM that she discovered Lord Mandelson had been granted high-level security clearance for his job as US ambassador despite vetting officials recommending against it.

Ms Badenoch tightened the thumb screws during PMQs, asking why Lord Mandelson was given access to highly classified briefings before he had received clearance.

Sir Keir hit back saying as a peer and privy counsellor Lord Mandelson could have access to material before developed vetting.

The defiant PM stuck to his guns throughout PMQs insisting that full due process was followed throughout Mandelson’s appointment.



And he insisted that Sir Olly should have told him that Foreign Office officials granted security clearance to Mandelson against the recommendation of UK Security Vetting.

He added: “Sir Olly Robbins was asked if he shared that decision with me, No 10 or any other ministers. He gave a clear answer: no. That puts to bed all the allegations levelled at me by those opposite in relation to dishonesty.”

Ms Badenoch described the PM’s answers as a “a joke” and quizzed him over claims No10 also tried to secure his former spin doctor Matthew Doyle an embassy job.

Sir Olly made the bombshell claim that No10 wanted to parachute Lord Doyle into a cushy diplomatic job.

Sir Olly claimed he was even told to keep this process secret from the then Foreign Secretary David Lammy.



Doyle was later made a peer before having to resign the Labour whip over his own relationship with a convicted paedophile.

Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey had another go to force an answer out of the PM on what he knew.

Sir Ed described Lord Doyle as “another Labour crony, friends with a convicted sex offender“.

He added: “Did he know his office was lobbying for a diplomatic job for Matthew Doyle, and were they doing it on his authority?”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Sir Keir swerved the question, reiterating that Lord Doyle had worked in public service for many years and “when people leave roles in any organisation, there are very often conversations about other roles they may want to apply for”.



Sir Ed said the House and public will note the PM “failed to answer my question”.

News.title: Teacher ‘who sexually abused and murdered baby he was adopting with boyfriend spoke of dark thoughts of drowning him’
News.content:
A TEACHER accused of sexually abusing and murdering a baby he was adopting told a colleague he had “dark thoughts” of drowning or suffocating him, a court heard.

Little Preston Davey was allegedly “routinely ill-treated” by Jamie Varley, who took indecent pictures and videos of the 13-month-old.





Varley, 37, allegedly smothered the baby to death by blocking his airways, Preston Crown Court heard.

Jurors heard following his death, one of Varley’s “close” colleagues went to police and told officers the teacher had visited her with Preston before the alleged murder and seemed “on edge”.

She said the baby’s arm was in a cast at the time after he broke his elbow, prosecutor Peter Wright KC said.



The prosecutor added: “He revealed to her he was struggling mentally. He was worried about [Preston] in respect of his not sleeping and that he was not bonding with him as he had hoped.

“He disclosed to her that he had harmful thoughts towards [Preston] and had thoughts of drowning him or suffocating him but that he would never carry them out.

“The witness tried to reassure him that such thoughts were capable of rational explanation and that sometimes as a parent you have thoughts of ‘worse case scenarios’.”

Varley and his partner John McGowan-Fazakerley are both accused of sexually assaulting Preston, who they were in the process of formally adopting.



Jurors heard McGowan-Fazakerley, 32, was aware of the psychological and physical abuse Varley was inflicting but allegedly “wilfully neglected to protect Preston”.

This allegedly included one occasion where Varley filmed Preston being spun so fast in a saucer at a play area on one occasion that his eyes appeared to go in different directions.

He also forced the tot to stay awake and filmed himself deliberately startling the baby, it was said.

The youngster was rushed to hospital on three occasions before his death suffering from breathing difficulties, seizures, a nose bleed and a fracture to his arm.

Staff noticed facial bruising but it was explained sufficiently by the defendants and he recovered quickly, the court heard.



In July last year, Varley allegedly caused Preston serious internal injuries after he sexually assaulted at home in Blackpool, Lancashire.

Jurors heard he then failed to call for help and instead caused the tot further harm.

A video later found on his phone showed Preston lying on a bed in respiratory arrest with his lips blue, it was said.

The court heard McGowan-Fazackerly had been at work and Varley was the sole carer for Preston that day.

He was eventually rushed to Blackpool Victoria Hospital where he died from an acute obstruction of his upper airway.



Jurors were told this was caused either a smothering with a hand or fabric or the insertion of an object into Preston’s mouth.

The baby also had 40 other traumatic injuries – including 30 external bruises, a fracture to his upper left arm and internal bruising to his mouth, throat and other parts of his body.

Mr Wright said: “As terrible as it is, this was not the result of some dreadful yet unforeseen accident or natural phenomenon.

“The evidence gathered during the investigation into his untimely death revealed a much more sinister pathology.

“We say the evidence demonstrates that he was murdered by one of the people entrusted with his well-being, one of his proposed adoptive parents, Jamie Varley.



“But this was not the only tragedy to befall him when in the care of these defendants. In the final moments of his short life, he was routinely ill treated, sexually abused and physically assaulted.”

Jurors heard Varley recorded some of the alleged abuse on his phone and shared it with McGowan-Fazackerly.

Mr Wright said this included a video of Preston “slithering and sliding in a bath” for 14 minutes while Varley failed to help him.

The prosecutor continued: “These are not happy snaps of a normal family life . They are indecent images.

“It is not difficult to distinguish between happy snaps and indecent images.”



The court heard Preston was born four weeks early and taken into local authority care at birth.

He lived happily with foster carers for the first nine months of his life while suitable adoptive parents were found.

Both Varley and McGowan-Fazackerly were both in a stable relationship and were keen to adopt a child, jurors were told.

They went through the adoption process from December 2021 to March 2022 and had been vetted well before Preston was born.

The couple visited Preston in February 2023 and he was assessed as “fit and healthy” with no underlying conditions, the court heard.



In March 2023, a proposed adoption was approved by the panel and he went to live with Varley and McGowan-Fazackerly the following month.

Varley denies murder, sexual assault of a child under 13, inflicting grievous bodily harm, five counts of child cruelty and further counts of making, taking and distributing indecent images.

McGowan-Fazakerley pleaded not guilty to causing and allowing the death of a child, two counts of child cruelty and sexual assault of a child under 13.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The trial continues.

News.title: Russian missiles flying near Chernobyl plant risking ‘major accident’ 40 years after nuclear catastrophe, Ukraine says
News.content:
RUSSIAN missiles flying near to the Chernobyl nuclear plant are risking a “major accident”, Ukraine has said.

A top state prosecutor claimed Russia has repeatedly piloted missiles and drones near the disused nuclear facility during waves of brutal attacks on Ukraine.





General Ruslan Kravchenko detailed previously unreported Russian military activity near the site as Ukraine prepares to mark the 40th anniversary of the 1986 disaster on Sunday.

Alongside Chernobyl, Ukraine is home to four nuclear power plants.



This includes Zaporizhzhia — Europe‘s largest – which has been under Russian control since the start of the invasion in 2022.

Both the Chernobyl and the Khmelnytskyi nuclear plant in western Ukraine have been on the flight path of Russian missiles, said Kravchenko.

As many as 35 Kinzhal missiles have been detected within 20km of either Chernobyl or the Khmelnytskyi sites.

Worse still, 18 of those missiles passed within 20km of both locations on the same flight.



“Such launches cannot be explained by any military considerations,” Kravchenko said.

“It is evident that the flights over the nuclear facilities are carried out solely for the purpose of intimidation or terror.”

In February last year, an object identified as a long-range Russian attack drone struck the facility, penetrating the radiation containment shield.

The Kremlin denied any involvement at the time, stating its forces do not target nuclear infrastructure.

Instead, it claimed Ukraine had carried out the attack themselves as a “provocation”.



More recently, Kravchenko said that Kinzhal missiles had fallen to the ground on three separate occasions.

The air-launched hypersonic missile that can carry a 500kg warhead landed within 10km of the Khmelnytskyi plant.



It remains unclear why the missiles came down, but Kravchenko said the wreckage did not suggest they were intercepted.

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) said it has “deep concern” about military activity in the vicinity of nuclear power plants.

The last of Chernobyl’s reactors was decommissioned in 2000 and the Zone Of Alienation around the plant has since become a popular tourist attraction.

In total, around 650,000 men volunteered to help contain the nuclear fallout when it happened.

Russian scientists estimate that up to 125,000 had died by 2005, but authorities deny a definite link between the number of fatalities and radiation exposure.



What happened at Chernobyl? WHEN an alarm bellowed out at the nuclear plant on April 26, 1986, workers looked on in horror as the control panels signaled a major meltdown in the number four reactor. The safety switches had been switched off in the early hours to test the turbine but the reactor overheated and generated a blast – the equivalent of 500 nuclear bombs. The reactor’s roof was blown off and a plume of radioactive material was blasted into the atmosphere. As air was sucked into the shattered reactor, it ignited flammable carbon monoxide gas causing a fire which burned for nine days. The catastrophe released at least 100 times more radiation than the atom bombs dropped on Nagasaki and Hiroshima. Soviet authorities waited 24 hours before evacuating the nearby town of Pripyat – giving the 50,000 residents just three hours to leave their homes. After the accident traces of radioactive deposits were found in Belarus where poisonous rain damaged plants and caused animal mutations. But the devastating impact was also felt in Scandinavia, Switzerland, Greece, Italy, France and the UK. An 18-mile radius known as the “Exclusion Zone” was set up around the reactor following the disaster. Most recently, on February 24, 2022 during the Russian invasion, Ukraine lost control over the Chernobyl site.

Petro Hurin, 76, is one of the few of liquidators still alive to this day.

He said his health was never the same after he was dispatched to the scene of the disaster.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He and 39 other workers were sent into the nuclear facility just a month after the explosion – today only five survive.

Petro said not a single worker who went to Chernobyl was ever in good health again.

News.title: Watch as giant tortoise is fitted with custom WHEELS by vets after struggling to walk
News.content:
THIS is the moment a giant tortoise walks again using an ingenious invention after struggling to move.

An Aldabra giant tortoise has been given a new lease of life after a genius vet fitted it with its very own set of custom wheels.





The tortoise had been struggling to move, with severe weakness in its back legs forcing it to drag itself along the ground.

It was a heartbreaking sight for his keepers, who knew they had to do something fast.

They rushed the giant creature in for urgent, specialist treatment.

Veterinarians carried out a full examination to get to the bottom of the mystery.



They feared the worst, but X-rays luckily showed no fractures or dislocations.

Experts believe the injury was likely caused by trauma, potentially during a scrap with other tortoises.

Dr Nielsen B Donato designed custom-made wheeled support to take the weight off the tortoise’s hind legs.

The innovative device allows the creature to move about far more freely.



A video of the amazing transformation was shared on April 8 and has since gone viral.

It has already racked up more than 100,000 likes and thousands of comments.

Dr Donato revealed the magic moment the tortoise was placed back on the ground, it began moving again with total ease.

He said he felt proud of both himself and his team as they watched it glide around the lab for the first time.

The tortoise is now back home continuing its recovery outdoors.



Getting back into the fresh air is key for the species to soak up the natural sunlight.

The vet says further treatment, such as laser therapy, could be used if needed to help bring down any inflammation.

The heartwarming procedure took place at a hospital in Taguig City, Philippines.

Fans online were quick to poke fun at the new set of wheels.

One joked: “After this, he will no longer be on turtle pace.”



Another quipped: “They see me rollin’. They hatin’.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A third viewer added: “Amazing. Feel like the wheels are a little too tall but what do I know.”

And a fourth laughed: “I am imagining one gets locked and the tortoise is just going around in circles. I shouldn’t laugh… Glad the tortoise is getting the care he needs though!”

News.title: Photos of pets outnumber snaps of family & partners on phones, survey reveals
News.content:
FURRY TAKEOVER Photos of pets outnumber snaps of family & partners on phones, survey reveals

THE average pet owner’s phone has 20 per cent more pictures of cats, dogs and other beloved animals – than their partners or dearest friends and family.

A poll of 2,000 with furry companions revealed they store an average of 176 snaps of four-legged friends on their device, compared to 147 pictures of their other half.





Pets also outnumber other loved ones, with respondents storing just 65 photos of their parents and 57 of their best friends on average.

It comes as 46 per cent of pet parents consider taking photos of something as a way of showing their love for it, with 40 per cent agreeing that a camera roll is a strong indicator of who or what people value the most.

Looking back on their camera roll makes more than half happy (51 per cent), while others feel nostalgic (36 per cent) and warm (33 per cent).

In fact, in the last month alone, 20 new pictures of pets have been added to camera rolls as 14 per cent snap pictures every single day – with these keen photographers taking around five photos daily.

Nearly seven in 10 (69 per cent) pet photographers added they are now using AI features or filters on their device to enhance pictures of their pets.

The research was commissioned by Samsung to celebrate the launch of the Galaxy A57 5G, which has Awesome Intelligence and ‘Fun Mode’ camera features that lets users use AR lenses to transform into different characters such as a pug or cat.

It also emerged Millennials have the most pet pictures on their phones, averaging 217 images, followed by Gen Z with 204, while Boomers trail behind on 103 snaps.

But overall, 52 per cent see their pet as a central member of the family, making them worthy of documenting at every opportunity.



When a pet is playing is the most likely moment to turn into a mini photoshoot (62 per cent), although 56 per cent can’t resist snapping a picture when their furry friend is fast asleep.

Despite 68 per cent preferring candid shots of their pet behaving naturally, 70 per cent still reach for their phone when their pet is doing something unusual or unexpected.

For nearly a quarter (23 per cent), these photos don’t just stay on their camera roll, with owners regularly sharing them on social media. And 48 per cent noticed pet pictures get more engagement than any other content they post.

News.title: Horror moment fairground reveller films as ride collapses after cables snap sending screaming revellers plummeting
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a fairground ride suddenly collapses mid-air sending riders plunging to the ground.

Dramatic video — taken by a passenger on the ride — captured the exact second the cables snap in the horror malfunction which left 11 people injured.





The phone camera footage begins with people laughing and enjoying the ride, which has passengers buckled into swing seats being swung in a circle.

Suddenly, all the seats crash to the ground as a loud mechanical sound can be heard and passengers scream.

Later, passengers can be seen lying on the floor of the platformed ride as they wait for medical attention.

Emergency services raced to the scene at Parque Las Vegas in Guaíba, southern Brazil, on Sunday 19 April, treating adults as well as children and teenagers.

Among those on board was Jeniffer Ferreira, 26, who escaped with minor injuries. She was taken to hospital and later discharged.

Her boyfriend, 28, suffered a fractured vertebra.

He was transferred to Hospital Cristo Redentor in nearby Porto Alegre but was also released the following day.



According to the fire department, the collapse happened after part of the structure – known as the tower – broke during the ride’s ascent.

One teenager who witnessed the incident said the attraction had been making “strange noises” moments before the collapse.

Investigators later found that two of the ride’s support cables had snapped, although it remains unclear if this directly caused the failure.

Police have also raised concerns over a lack of maintenance records, suggesting the equipment may have been in a “very precarious” condition.

The park, which had only opened in the city on March 14 and was due to run until April 26, was immediately shut down.



In a statement, Parque Las Vegas said it “deeply regrets” what happened and is assisting victims and their families, insisting it complies with all safety regulations.

The attraction had been operating in the car park of a Havan store, though the retailer stressed it has no connection to the park and that it operates independently.

Local authorities confirmed the site had the necessary permits but said operations have been suspended as a precaution while the investigation continues.

News.title: Evil foster mum allowed her son to rape me & film abuse from the age of 5… there was a shocking reason she walked free
News.content:
COWERING in bed, Amanda Brown sobbed as she heard the door open again. The little girl, who had been taken away from her mother at just six months old, was being abused by her evil foster family.

The Robertsons subjected her and other children in their care to years of physical, sexual and mental abuse. Now, after 30 years, Amanda has finally faced her abusers in court. Bravely waving her anonymity, she tells the Sun the horror of her ordeal, and why the outcome of her court case is ‘disgusting’ and ‘disappointing’.





Amanda, now 38, went into the care of Jennifer Robertson, now 79, when she was just six months old, after social services took her away from her biological mother.

She lived with the Robertsons until the age of five, and during that time suffered a string of physical assaults from Jennifer, whilst her son Steven, now 52, and her late husband sexually assaulted and raped her.

The mother and son were both sentenced at the High Court in Edinburgh this week, but Jennifer avoided jail time, which Amanda says is “not justice at all”.

“All I ever knew was abuse, at the time I thought it was normal,” Amanda tells the Sun.

I don’t know how we survived. Jennifer knew that he was doing this to me

“I just thought it happened to everybody. Steven would sexually assault me and another victim to perform with me – it was to the point I was bleeding.

“It was a repeated cycle of Steven coming to my bedroom at night. I don’t remember a day when I wasn’t getting hurt.

“Looking back on it now, I don’t know how we survived. Jennifer knew that he was doing this to me.”

Amanda says Jennifer would also punch her in the stomach and hold her head under the water during bathtime to stop her from breathing.





During the same time period, her son Steven preyed on her by repeatedly kissing her on the mouth, chest and private parts.

In one particularly evil act, he induced her to commit a sex act on him and another youngster.

“I just feel like they only stole my childhood; they’ve stolen these years trying to get justice. I just want to be able to live.”

“This has been my whole life.”

When she got to the Robertsons’ house in Murthly, Perthshire, Scotland, Steven was a teenager.

Amanda says she does not know when the abuse began, as she was a baby when she went into their household.

Steven targeted girls who had been placed in his mother’s care at the family home.

He sexually assaulted Amanda while acting with his now deceased father, Alan Robertson, in the 1980s and 1990s.

All the children were under the age of five when he began abusing them.



“I never said stop,” Amanda adds in tears.

“I just stood there and cried, and at the end, I would be told to clean myself up, and an older sibling who lived in the property would clean me up.

“It was painful, I can remember the pain to this day. It was excruciating, and that pain affected me right through my life.

“Steven’s assaults were filmed on his VHS camera. I was under the impression that he would hand these out to people. So I never felt at ease to speak out.”

‘It was like hell, a house of horrors’

Living in the house was “like hell” to Amanda, who said there was “no love” in the family.

Her foster mother, Jennifer, subjected the children to cruel and unnatural treatment, which included forcing some children to wear urine-soaked underwear on their heads and to sit in cold baths.

“My flashbacks are only of the punishments of being forced to eat beans, she would punch me, and there was one incident where she held me under the water, and she kept pushing me back and forth into the water,”

“The house was like I was in hell, there was nowhere I could turn to in that house and feel like you were safe.



“When I see my children, I light up, and I’m excited to give them a cuddle; it was not like that.

“You’d be assaulted, there was a lack of food, and there was no safe space there.”

Jennifer was found guilty of verbally and physically abusing three children, and of failing to take steps to prevent the assault and sexual abuse of another child by her son.

Amanda explained that at the age of five, the process of her being adopted began, but Jennifer and Steven were still involved in her life.

She says: “I had to go back to their house because the three years of paperwork of adoption had not been finalised.

‘My adoptive parents saved my life’

“My adoptive parents felt they were under threat because she would say I would go back to adoption.

“My adoptive family felt straight away that something wasn’t right.

“I’d walk into the door, and Jennifer would punch me straight in the stomach.

“My adoptive family were coming up to pick me up, and my hair was a mess, and my clothes weren’t done properly.”

Amanda claims that when the paperwork was finally completed, her adoptive mum took her to the police, and it was found that she had internal damage.



“It took me a year to disclose everything to my adoptive family. I didn’t really trust the police, so I didn’t say much to them.

“After coming to me, three weeks after they stopped investigating.

“I felt like I was not being heard by the police. I felt like if I said something, I’d be in trouble.

“It was only when I got adopted that I was like ‘why aren’t you hurting me?’ To me, it was normal. My adoptive parents saved my life.

“They did everything in their power to stand beside me to make sure my voice got heard. I could not have wished for a better family.

“I stayed with them from 8 until I was 16. To this day, I class them as my mum and dad.”

Last week, Steven Robertson was jailed for 11 years with a further three-year sentence extension during which time he will be subject to close monitoring and supervision.

His name has been added to the sex offenders register indefinitely.



‘It wasn’t a fair outcome – it’s disgusting’

Jennifer Robertson was given a Community Payback Order with conduct requirements and ordered to perform 250 hours of unpaid work within 12 months.

Judge John Morris KC said: “It is clear that your victims have suffered severe harm and continue to suffer severe trauma.

“You have a complete lack of remorse even for the things you admit doing.”

Sentencing Jennifer Robertson, he acknowledged her age, that she’s a fall risk and added: “I am well aware that your victims want you to go to prison.

“However, I am narrowly persuaded to draw back from sending you to prison. I am persuaded in the circumstances that I can draw back from custody and to impose a community payback order.

“Such a sentence is a direct alternative to custody. It is designed to be an onerous sentence.

“Should you not comply with any part of the sentence, you will be brought back before me and you can be sent to prison.”

Non-harassment orders, banning both individuals from contacting or attempting to contact the victims, were also granted indefinitely.

Victims were seen shouting and crying in the courtroom when Jennifer’s sentencing was given.

Amanda says she felt “let down” that Jennifer did not get jail time.



She is just going to be living her life as norma

“I don’t think it was a fair outcome. For her to walk away freely is just disgusting.

“We relieved everything, and where has this really got us? I just feel disappointed.

“Towards Steven, I feel like I had some sort of justice, but with Jennifer, it doesn’t feel like it.

“She is just going to be living her life as normal. I don’t think her age should be taken into consideration; she didn’t care about our ages at the time of the abuse.”

In 2018, the Scottish Police came to her house following abuse claims related to Jennifer and Steven.

“In my heart, I knew that someone had spoken up, and if I had the choice to relieve this, I wouldn’t have chosen to, but I knew who it was and that needed help.”

Jennifer and Steven Robertson were found guilty of a total of nine charges on March 20.

The Crown led evidence from the victims, who gave consistent accounts describing a pattern of offending behaviour by Jennifer.



Amanda said the abuse affected her self-worth and that for a long time, she never valued herself.

“I just allowed men to take what they wanted from me because I didn’t feel like I was worthy of love,” she said.

I can honestly say that if it hadn’t been for my children, I wouldn’t be here today

“Throughout my life growing up, I just never had a voice. That was taken from me at such a young age.

“It’s always been so chaotic because I spent so long trying to be heard, and the last seven years, this has come back again.

“While trying to support my family, I also had to fight this battle. It’s been a journey on its own.”

Amanda’s children, aged four to 20 years old, are her “reason for living”, she said.

“I can honestly say that if it hadn’t been for my children, I wouldn’t be here today.

“When I was older, and I struggled to cope in my teens, I used to drink a lot.

“Now I want to be able to move forward. I want my children and myself to have the best life.

“I feel like now my voice has been heard, I can settle down.”



Police Scotland’s Detective Constable Ursula Honeyman says: “Jennifer Robertson had a duty of care to these children.

“She not only neglected them but did nothing when her son sexually abused them.

“Steven Robertson systematically abused young girls staying at his family home over a number of years and now faces the consequences of his depraved actions.”

Faye Cook, Procurator Fiscal for High Court Sexual Offences, says:

“Jennifer Robertson had a clear duty to protect the young people in her care and to keep them safe as an approved foster carer.

“Instead, she caused profound harm through sustained cruelty and abuse, including enabling others to sexually abuse the children.

“Steven Robertson’s predatory behaviour went unchecked, allowing him to systematically abuse and rape these young girls over a number of years.

“Their actions have had lifelong consequences for those affected, and I am grateful to the survivors for the courage they have shown throughout the prosecution process.”

News.title: Neurologist's supplement warning as common vitamin could be 'toxic'
News.content:
Neurologist's supplement warning as common vitamin could be 'toxic'

A neurologist has warned that taking too much of this vitamin can lead to peripheral neuropathy and nerve damage

View 3 Images A doctor has issued a warning about a popular supplement (Image: Getty)

A neurologist has issued a warning that a widely-used supplement could turn "toxic". The expert says consuming excessive amounts of this vitamin could lead to damaged sensory neurons.

‌



Our bodies depend on specific vitamins and minerals to function at their best. While the majority of our nutritional needs are met through a healthy, balanced diet, certain people may require daily supplements.

‌



Yet there are important cautions surrounding supplement use. In a video shared on social media platform TikTok, a neurologist elaborated further.

‌



Dr Baibing Chen, widely known as Dr Bing, explained that certain vitamins can prove "toxic". He said: "A lot of people think that because vitamins are natural and you can get them over the counter, they can't cause you any harm, but that's not completely true.

"Some vitamins can absolutely be toxic. For example, vitamins A, D, E, and K. These are fat-soluble vitamins and can build up in your body.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



"And even water-soluble vitamins like vitamins B and C, which you think that you're supposed to be able to just pee out, are not always harmless."

Particularly, he highlighted vitamin B6. Also referred to as pyridoxine, B6 is essential for the body to utilise and store energy from protein and carbohydrates in food.

It also enables the body to produce haemoglobin, the substance in red blood cells responsible for transporting oxygen throughout the body. B6 occurs naturally in foods including pork, poultry, peanuts, soya beans, oats, and bananas. Dr Bing continued: "One that surprises people is vitamin B6, and you can overdose on it.

‌



"I've seen this several times as a neurologist, and at high levels, B6 becomes more toxic, and it disrupts normal neuronal signalling and can overstimulate and damage sensory neurons, which then lead to degeneration of those nerve fibres."

View 3 Images It is possible to take too much of this supplement, he said (Image: Getty)

This can trigger symptoms such as peripheral neuropathy. Dr Bing said: "That's why patients will develop numbness, tingling, burning, pain, and balance problems because the brain is getting distorted or incomplete sensory input."

‌



However, he explained that this risk doesn't stem from just one large dose of B6. "The biggest issue is not someone taking a massive dose at once, but it's rather stacking," he said.

"I had a young patient taking multivitamins plus energy drinks every day, plus an anti-stress supplement, plus a sleep supplement. None of them seem extreme, but they all had B6 and he had no idea, and he ended up with neuropathy.

"Even after stopping it, recovery is not always complete. Now, to be clear, I'm not against supplements; I recommend them to patients when they're indicated, and I take some myself.

‌



"But it needs to be individualised. And we need to be smart about it and be evidence-based."

View 3 Images An excess of vitamin B6 can result in peripheral neuropathy (Image: Getty)

What does the NHS say?

His guidance is supported by the NHS website, which cautions that excessive B6 can result in peripheral neuropathy. It states: "Taking 200mg or more a day of vitamin B6 can lead to a loss of feeling in the arms and legs known as peripheral neuropathy.

‌



"This will usually improve once you stop taking the supplements. But in a few cases when people have taken large amounts of vitamin B6, particularly for more than a few months, the effect can be permanent.

"The effect of taking vitamin B6 at doses between 10mg and 200mg is unclear. So there's not enough evidence to say how long these doses could be taken for safely."

Article continues below

The health body advises that you should not consume more than 10mg of vitamin B6 daily in supplements unless recommended by a doctor.

News.title: Michael Antonio's Lamborghini clocked speeding just three months after surviving life-threatening horror crash
News.content:
Michael Antonio's Lamborghini clocked speeding just three months after surviving life-threatening horror crash

A Lamborghini belonging to ex-West Ham striker Michail Antonio was clocked speeding - just months after he was pulled from the twisted wreckage of his £260,000 Ferrari

View 3 Images Michail Antonio is facing a driving ban for failing to tell police who was driving his Lamborghini when it was clocked speeding (Image: Getty Images)

Ex-West Ham United striker Michail Antonio is facing a driving ban after his Lamborghini was clocked speeding - just months after he survived a horror crash.

‌



The former Premier League ace, 36, was found guilty in his absence of failing to tell police who was driving the motor when it was caught travelling at an average of 50mph in a 40mph zone last year. A charge of speeding was dropped by prosecutors as magistrates heard that Antonio's Lamborghini Urus was exceeded the speed limit on Lee Bank Middleway and Belgrave Middleway in Birmingham on March 1 last year.

‌



The incident came just three months after Antonio, who now plays for a club in the Qatar Stars League, was pulled from the twisted wreckage of his Ferrari when it smashed into a tree in Essex. He spent three weeks in hospital in December 2024 and suffered a badly broken leg after the smash left his £260,000 supercar a mangled wreck.

‌



View 3 Images Antonio survived a horror crash in Epping when his powerful Ferrari was left a mangled wreck by the side of the road (Image: UKNIP)

Today Birmingham Magistrates' Court was told he already has six points on his licence, including for having no insurance at the time of the crash. He now faces a further six penalty points for failing to notify police of the identity of the driver of the Lamborghini, meaning he would be disqualified from driving under "totting up" procedures. Antonio, who also played for Reading, Nottingham Forest, Southampton and Sheffield Wednesday, will be sentenced by magistrates in Birmingham on June 19.

A 12-minute hearing today was told a letter asking for information about the driver of the Urus was sent by West Midlands Police to Antonio's home in Beaconsfield, Buckinghamshire, three days after it was clocked speeding. Prosecutor Lucy Allen told the magistrates hearing the case: "There has been no response received to that notice. We offer no evidence in relation to the speeding offence."

‌



Magistrates did not retire before convicting Antonio of failing to provide information on April 4 last year. Jamaica international Antonio was not legally represented at the hearing, with the court clerk telling magistrates: "The defendant has not put forward a reason for you to consider (for failing to provide information)."

View 3 Images Antonio, who now plays for a club in the Qatar Stars League, did not appear in court in Birmingham today (Image: PA)

The three magistrates presiding over the case were also told that Antonio had provided no details of his income. In a separate case, Antonio is accused of failing to respond to the Metropolitan Police over an allegation of driving without due care and attention in central London.

‌



Police say the footballer was the registered keeper of a Lamborghini Urus which is accused of being involved in an incident on Pall Mall at 12.38am on November 5 last year. Antonio was written to by the Met and asked to identify the driver of the car, and he allegedly failed to respond, sparking a criminal prosecution.

Court papers do not reveal what the Lamborghini was accused of doing on Pall Mall. In his response to the prosecution, Antonio entered a not guilty plea to the charge of failing to give information relating to the identification of the driver of a vehicle when required. He wrote: "The vehicle was on hire at the time of contravention. I have the hire agreement as proof."

The prosecution was brought through the Single Justice Procedure, with a magistrate sitting in private to handle cases on the papers. A court official said the Pall Mall-related case has now been adjourned for a public hearing on July 7 at Bexley Magistrates' Court.

Article continues below

Speaking in January last year, Antonio told the BBC he had been given "another chance at life" after the Epping Forest crash, which left him "close to dying". Antonio has also previously spoken of crashing a Lamborghini Huracan into a bin shed while dressed as a snowman, on what he described as a "slippery road" in London on Christmas Day 2019.

News.title: B&M's 'modern' £30 table set similar to £90 Argos version 'adds style to rooms'
News.content:
B&M's 'modern' £30 table set similar to £90 Argos version 'adds style to rooms'

People could be getting much more for their money

View 3 Images The B&M set is £55 cheaper than a single version sold by Argos (Image: Getty)

People could inject a "clean and natural" touch to homes with a living room set that B&M claims to "complement most interiors". Shoppers might want to consider this bundle when updating their spaces, as it's more budget-friendly than other stores' bundles.

‌



Describing the set online, B&M bosses wrote: "Add versatility and modern style to your living room with this Home Collection Set of Two Tables. Featuring a modern panelled style with a clean and natural finish, this pair of tables effortlessly elevates any living space and complements most interiors."

‌



The discount store claimed that the set of tables would be perfectly suited to being "side tables or lamp tables". The smaller of the pair stands 31cm tall with a surface area of 34cm, and the second table is slightly taller at 38cm with a surface area of 40cm.

‌



The set of two is new to B&M and available in stores for £35. This modern design is not exclusive to the store; other brands offer something similar for much more money.

For example, Argos is selling a single Habitat Luan Slatted Side Table for £90 (offered via click-and-collect or home delivery). The deal already looks better at B&M, since shoppers can claim two tables for £55 less than the single-table version at Argos.

View 3 Images The Home Collection Set of Two Tables (Image: B&M)

‌



Describing the Luan piece online, Argos bosses said: "It is solid wood with a clean white painted finish that brings a calm, Nordic-inspired feel to your living room or bedroom. The slatted design adds a bit of character while staying practical and unfussy.

"It sits comfortably next to your favourite armchair or sofa, fitting into relaxed, modern spaces without taking over. The slatted design keeps things light and airy rather than blocky."

The homeware store confirms online that the Argos version is larger than the bigger B&M table, measuring 50cm tall and having a table surface of 50cm too. It also claims to be made from "solid wood" as opposed to B&M's version, which is made from MDF.

‌



View 3 Images The Habitat Luan Slatted Side Table (Image: Argos)

Shoppers looking to renovate a room on a budget might be drawn to affordable options at shops like B&M and Home Bargains. In some cases, items may be virtually identical to more expensive brands but at a fraction of the cost, which few would know unless you told them.

One other example of this is the deal on curtains at Home Bargains. The discount chain has an £8 offer on its Home Collections Blackout Single Curtain, which looks very similar to a more expensive Dunelm version costing £17 more.

Article continues below

Elsewhere, shoppers may still be able to find the £18 Ania Glass Ball Lamp that our shopping writers thought was a near identical match to something from Oliver Bonas, worth £99. The "stylish and decorative piece" was "designed to complement any traditional or modern home".

News.title: Conductor knocks priceless violin out of musician's hands and sends it crashing to the floor
News.content:
Conductor knocks priceless violin out of musician's hands and sends it crashing to the floor

Soloist Elina Vahala was playing the finale of a concerto during a Sinfonia Lahti concert in Finland when enthusiastic conductor Matthew Halls knocked the 18th century instrument from her hands

Conductor knocks a priceless violin out of a soloist's hands

The dramatic moment a conductor accidentally knocks a priceless 18th century violin out of a soloist's hands sending it crashing to the floor has been captured on camera.

‌



The incident unfolded during a Sinfonia Lahti concert in Finland while violinist Elina Vahala played the finale of a concerto last Thursday. Conductor Matthew Halls accidentally struck the instrument as he enthusiastically led the orchestra - sending it flying out of Elina's grip and toward the floor.

‌



She appears totally shocked, with her hands jumping to cover her face as the violin flips in the air several times. But Elina was able to react in a split-second, getting her foot underneath the violin, softening the impact and preventing what could have been catastrophic damage.

‌



View 3 Images Elina had been playing the finale of the concerto when the accident happened (Image: CEN)

Naples tourist on dream birthday holiday killed walking down street after teen hurls statue off balcony READ MORE :

She then looks down in complete horror at the instrument lying on the ground. The orchestra continues playing until Mr Halls motions for them to stop while Elina crouches down to retrieve her beloved instrument.

The instrument in question is a rare violin which was made by Italian master Giovanni Battista Guadagnini in the 18th century. Similar instruments have been valued at between one and three million euros (£869,000 to £2.6million).

‌



View 3 Images Elina Vahala looked down in horror as her instrument lay on the floor (Image: CEN)

After the shocking accident, the concert was briefly paused while the valuable violin was checked before it was returned to Elina so the concert could continue. Though the violin appeared intact, the musician later said the sound had changed slightly, suggesting a small internal shift or a loosened seam.

"It was an incredible reflect that I managed to get my foot in the way," Elina said. She added that she does not actually remember the moment itself and only noticed it later when she watched the video back.

‌



View 3 Images The violin was checked out before being given back to Elina for the performance to continue (Image: CEN)

She went on to explain that the violin is more than just a valuable instrument, describing it as being a "part of her". She said the violin has adapted to her playing style over many years, explaining: "It's an organis part of me".

The instrument was later spent to a specialist for repair, who confirmed that the damage was minor and involved a seam that had come loose. Violin maker Jarkko Niemi said the outcome could have been far worse, noting that such falls can easily cause cracks or even break the neck of a violin.

Article continues below

Conductor Halls apologised for the accident, while the orchestra showed its support for the soloist. Elina said she holds no grudges and hopes to carry on performing with her restored instrument at upcoming concerts.

News.title: Security guard left with life-changing injuries after X Factor finalist Gabrielle Carrington crash
News.content:
Security guard left with life-changing injuries after X Factor finalist Gabrielle Carrington crash

Security guard Anoosh Chaichy, 56, was left with life-changing injuries when he and an influencer were allegedly mowed down outside a London nightclub by an X Factor finalist

View 5 Images Anoosh Chaichy, 56, was standing next to an e-scooter when he was struck by a Mercedes (Image: Instagram)

A security guard who suffered life-changing injuries after he was allegedly struck by an influencer behind the wheel of a Mercedes has been pictured.

‌



Anoosh Chaichy, 56, from Edgware, in north London, had been standing next to BBL influencer Klaudiaglam, real name Klaudia Zakrzewska, while he attempted to move his e-scooter when both were struck by the black vehicle. The security guard was left lying on the pavement while Klaudia was taken to hospital in a critical condition following the incident outside a nightclub in London on Sunday night.

‌



X Factor finalist-turned-influencer Gabrielle Carrington, 29, who is also known as RIELLEUK online, was apprehended and charged with attempted murder, grievous bodily harm with intent, actual bodily harm as well as dangerous driving.

‌



View 5 Images Anoosh worked as a security guard (Image: Instagram)

Polish-born Klaudia, who boasts nearly 260,000 followers on Instagram, had been at the Inca nightclub on Saturday night before the incident took place. Carrington appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Tursday where District Judge Nina Tempia remanded her in custody. Carrington is a former member of Miss Dynamix who made it to the X Factor finals in 2013, now she has more than 365,000 followers online.

View 5 Images Anoosh was struck by a vehicle outside a Soho nightclub (Image: Instagram)

‌



Outlining the allegations against Carrington, prosecutor Rizwan Amin told the court: "In the early hours of Sunday morning, April 19, ambulance services and police were called to Argyll Street for reports that a woman had been run over. Officers had attended at 5am, and also London Ambulance Service were on the scene."

Mr Amin went on to outline what the prosecution claims to be the seuqnce of events which, he said, left Anoosh Chaichy and a Ms Latisha Armstrong injured along with Ms Zakrzewska.

View 5 Images Anoosh was left with life-changing injuries (Image: Instagram)

‌



"Police attended with the London Ambulance Service, a woman in her 30’s remains in a life-threatening condition," a Met Police spokesperson said. "In the same collision, a man in his 50s sustained life-changing injuries and was taken to hospital. A third woman, aged in her 30s, was treated for minor injuries."

Detective Chief Inspector Alison Foxwell, of Specialist Crime South, said: "As our enquiries continue, our thoughts are with those injured and their loved ones. While this incident took place in the early hours of the morning, venues in the area were still open, and we believe a number of people will have seen what happened. I would urge anyone who witnessed the collision, or any activity prior to it that they feel may be of relevance, to come forward."

View 5 Images Carrington has been charged following the collision (Image: rielleuk/Instagram)

‌



Carrington, of Manchester, has been charged with attempted murder, causing grievous bodily harm with intent, assault occasioning actual bodily harm, dangerous driving and drink driving. She did not enter any pleas during Tuesday's court hearing.

After the charges were announced, David Malone, deputy chief crown prosecutor for the CPS in London North, said: “We remind all concerned that proceedings against the defendant are active and that she has the right to a fair trial. It is vital that there should be no reporting, commentary, or sharing of information online which could in any way prejudice these proceedings."

Article continues below

The investigation continues and those will relevant information can upload it to the major incident portal here, or contact police on 101, providing the reference 3374/19APR. Information can also be provided to the independent charity Crimestoppers, anonymously, on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Fears raised Donald Trump could embarrass the King during US state visit
News.content:
Fears raised Donald Trump could embarrass the King during US state visit

The chair of the Foreign Affairs Committee raised concerns that the US President 'can't stop himself', and claimed she was 'worried' about the King and Queen heading to America

View 2 Images Emily Thornberry raised concerns over King Charles meeting with Donald Trump (Image: AP)

Donald Trump could use an upcoming state visit to embarrass the King, Emily Thornberry has warned.

‌



The chair of the Foreign Affairs Committee raised concerns that the US President “ can’t stop himself", and claimed she was “worried” about the King and Queen heading to America.

‌



The pair will meet with Trump in person five times over four days as they try to repair the strained relations between the US and UK amid the conflict in Iran.

‌



Nigel Farage and Kemi Badenoch mocked in Donald Trump balloon stunt READ MORE :

View 2 Images Emily Thornberry is an outspoken critic of Donald Trump (Image: Thomas Krych/ZUMA Press Wire/REX/Shutterstock)

Ms Thornberry, an outspoken critic of the US President, described the visit as “high stakes”. She said: “At the moment I have reservations about it. My worry is that they'll be embarrassed, my worry is Trump's behaviour, and my worry is that it's against a backdrop of there being a war and I hope that it's been thought through very carefully and that there aren't opportunities for Trump to embarrass their majesties.

Article continues below

“I worry about him saying something to the media, the media shout out questions to him all the time, and he can’t stop himself answering. At 4:00 in the morning when he's over excited, I just don't know what he might write. “He seems to think the King is a personal friend, and that the King is the one who wants to come. The King is probably being a proper public servant and doing the right thing. I worry about it, it’s high stakes.”

Donald Trump has already been handed two state visits to the UK, but this is the first time a British monarch has visited the US since Queen Elizabeth in 2007. Tensions have been particularly high between Trump and Keir Starmer, with the president calling the UK’s approach to the Iran war “terrible” and labelling the PM as “no Winston Churchill”.

Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey has called on the PM to call off the royal state visit, which will mark the start of the 250th anniversary of American independence. Speaking last week, he said: “President Trump is one of the most unpredictable people we have seen on the world stage and I hope he does not embarrass our monarch”.

News.title: Woman to run London Marathon in memory of all women killed by men after best pal bludgeoned by husband
News.content:
Woman to run London Marathon in memory of all women killed by men after best pal bludgeoned by husband

Hetti Barkworth-Nanton - who was the last person to speak to "soul mate" Joanna Simpson before she was killed - will run 26.2miles through the capital in memory of all the women who killer by a man last year

View 5 Images Hetti Barkworth-Nanton will wear a pink cape decorated with butterflies to represent every woman killed by a man in the UK in 2025 (Image: PA)

The best friend of slain Joanna Simpson will take part in the London Marathon in memory of every woman killed by a man last year.

‌



Hetti Barkworth-Nanton, 59, was the last person to speak to "soul mate" Joanna Simpson before she was brutally killed by her husband in 2010. She has tirelessly fought for BA pilot Robert Brown to remain behind bars after he was jailed for manslaughter. Now Hetti will run 26.2miles wearing a pink bespoke cape decorated with butterflies to represent every woman killed by a man in the UK in 2025.

‌



She aims to boost public awareness of the tragic reality that on average one woman is killed by a partner or ex-partner in England and Wales every five days and more than 100 women were killed by men last year. Hetti, the chair of trustees at charity Refuge, said: “I started my training back in November, knowing there were women still alive who would be represented on this cape. That was almost unbearable to comprehend – but it’s also exactly why it’s so vital to improve public awareness.

‌



View 5 Images Joanna Simpson, 46, was bludgeoned death at her home in Windsor, Berks, within earshot of her children (Image: PA)

"The London Marathon is a hugely powerful way to force the fatal consequences of domestic abuse into public view, ensuring we can reach people who might not otherwise engage with conversations about VAWG." Ex-British Airways captain Brown, 61, will go before a Parole Board panel within days. The hearing will be held in private after justice officials declined a request to make it public - despite Joanna's mum, Diana Parkes, saying she was "terrified" at the prospect of Brown walking free.

Last week the Mirror revealed Brown will be quizzed by Parole Board professionals over two days on April 23 and 24. Today Hetti said: "The upcoming parole hearing of Robert Brown, who killed my dear friend Jo Simpson, serves as a stark reminder that sadly, a sentence is rarely the end. For those bereaved by domestic abuse, parole can be deeply re-traumatising, forcing loved ones to relive their loss and the trauma that surrounds it all over again. It feels like more than a coincidence that this is all happening at the same time – with the parole hearing set to take place just two days before the London Marathon.

‌



View 5 Images Robert Brown was jailed for 26 years for manslaughter after he killed his wife, Joanna, in their family home in 2010 (Image: PA)

"This isn’t just about running a marathon – it’s about making sure that we remember the life of every woman who has been killed because of male violence. As services like Refuge face an underfunding crisis, this is also a critical time for fundraising to ensure that all survivors of abuse can access the lifesaving support they need and deserve.”

Brown bludgeoned Joanna, 46, to death at her Windsor, Berks, home within earshot of their children. It followed years of domestic abuse and was within a week of their divorce being finalised. He then buried her in a pre-dug grave at Great Windsor Park. Brown was jailed for 26 years for manslaughter, after arguing that he was suffering from adjustment disorder at the time of the attack.

‌



View 5 Images Hetti has tirelessly fought to raise awareness around domestic violence ever since Joanna was killed by her husband

He was due to be freed last year but his early release was blocked by Justice Secretary Alex Chalk. In early 2024, Brown launched a legal challenge against the government’s decision to block his release, claiming the intervention was "politically motivated". The High Court dismissed Brown’s judicial review in February 2024.

Mr Justice Ritchie ruled that the Justice Secretary had "reasonable grounds" to believe Brown posed a significant risk of serious harm to the public. During the Judicial Review, the court heard Brown showed "no remorse" and could be at risk of killing again. The MoJ argued he was a "significant risk of serious harm" due to "non-engagement" with probation officers. He had also not completed accredited courses to recognise his offending.

‌



View 5 Images Hetti has forged a close bond with Joanna's mother, Diana Parkes, as the pair fight to keep Brown in prison (Image: Daily Mirror)

In January 2007, Joanna went to a solicitor after Brown accused her of having an affair. Eventually, the couple split and Joanna was encouraged by the outcome Radmacher v Granatino case, which saw prenups being seen as enforceable in the UK. Her parents had encouraged her to sign a prenup with Brown. However, Joanna was killed by Brown on October 31, 2010.

Brown phoned the police about a “serious domestic incident” and was arrested on suspicion of being involved in Joanna’s death. He accompanied police when they recovered Joanna’s body from the woodland area where he disposed of her body.

Article continues below

After Joanna's death, Hetti fought to end the misery of domestic violence. Ahead of this weekend's London Marathon, Refuge released a new film which sees Hetti joined by broadcaster Julie Etchingham and Refuge ambassadors including David Morrissey, Ranvir Singh, Lorien Haynes and Sharon Gaffka on a training run in central London, in solidarity with her powerful tribute to victims of domestic homicide and male violence against women.

To sponsor Hetti go to www.justgiving.com/page/hetti-barkworth-nanton-2

News.title: Moment plane crashes into power cables and nosedives into Los Angeles car park
News.content:
Moment plane crashes into power cables and nosedives into Los Angeles car park

Dashcam footage shows the moment a light aircraft hit power cables in the Pacoima area of Los Angeles before plunging from the sky - the pilot was rushed to hospital

View 3 Images The plane was seen falling from the sky (Image: X)

Huge sparks could be seen as a plane hit power cables before nosediving and crashing into a car park.

‌



Footage from a vehicle dashcam showed how the light aircraft was flying low and collided with electricity lines as it crossed over a road and caused massive sparks in the Pacoima area of Los Angeles.

‌



The pilot appeared to be helpless as the plane descended vertically into the car park of O’Reilly Auto Parts while people rushed to try and help. The plane is understood to have taken off from Whiteman Airport and crashed shortly after 11am on Monday near the junction between San Fernando Road and Van Nuys Boulevard.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Emergency services rushed to the scene and a Los Angeles Fire Department spokesman said the 72-year-old pilot had already been removed from the plane when they arrived.

Around a dozen people could be seen lifting up a wing of the aircraft to help the pilot from underneath. He was rushed to hospital in a critical condition.

‌



“Me and my brother and like 10 other people helped pick up the plane and rescued the guy out,” Luz De La Cruz told KTLA-TV. “It was very terrifying.”

View 3 Images Emergency services examining the plane (Image: AP)

Electricity had to be cut to the area due to the hazard caused by loose cables. A police cordon was put in place for the nearby roads.

‌



“All these wires were coming down,” Ms De La Cruz said. “You could see the sparks in them, so the people from O’Reilly’s ran outside and were screaming at us like, get off the cars, it’s going to spark on your cars.”

The Federal Aviation Administration said it was investigating the crash and identified the fixed-wing plane as a Cessna 172 S Skyhawk SP, reported the Los Angeles Times.

View 3 Images The plane landed in a car park (Image: KTLA 5)

‌



Flight Radar 24 shows the plane took off from Whiteman Airport shortly before 11am. It appears that the plane was in the air for less than 10 minutes when it turned around and headed back to the airport before crashing.

The plane had been rented out to the pilot according to the Whiteman Airport Coalition, an advocacy group for the airport. “Events like this are taken very seriously,” it wrote. “Whiteman Airport operates under strict federal safety standards, with rigorous requirements for pilot training, aircraft maintenance, and flight operations.”

There have been concerns about the safety at the small airport in the past. After a crash in January 2022, the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors reportedly looked into closing the airport and in April that year a pilot died when a Cessna crashed alongside the 210 Freeway in Sylmar after taking off from Whiteman Airport.

Article continues below

Also in November 2020, a Cessna crashed in a residential area near the airport’s runway, killing a Civil Air Patrol pilot.

Travelers are increasingly worried about the cost and availability of flights for spring and summer trips as the U.S. and Israel's war with Iran squeezes global oil supplies.

The head of the International Energy Agency warned last week that European countries could run low on jet fuel within weeks, forcing the continent's airlines and carriers that fly to Europe to significantly reduce flights.

Many airlines have already raised checked bag fees or added fuel surcharges as the global price of jet fuel increased from about $99 per barrel at the end of February to as high as $209 a barrel at the beginning of April.

In a sign of the conflict’s ongoing repercussions for travel, Air Canada said Friday that it will suspend service to New York’s John F. Kennedy International Airport from June 1 until Oct. 25 to lower its fuel costs.

Other airlines, ranging from U.S. carriers like United and Delta to Air France-KLM, SAS, Philippine Airlines and and Cathay Pacific in Europe and Asia, have reduced routes and either increased ticket prices or said they would hike them if the war keeps oil from passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

“It’s very hard for the airlines to make predictions in this environment, so they’re going to be conservative, and that’s why it’s likely that their prices will remain elevated for some time until things really stabilize,” said Shye Gilad, a former airline captain who now teaches at Georgetown University’s business school.

open image in gallery One of the easiest ways to save money is to pack light ( Getty Images )

With airfares and fees on the rise, consumers still can make choices that determine how much of their travel budgets will get taken up by paying to get to and from their destinations.

Act quickly

While consumers may be tempted to see if the war ends before buying airline tickets, the “wait-and-see" approach to booking flights is riskier this year, travel experts say, especially the longer the war goes on and the closer to summer and other peak travel periods it gets.

“Presuming there is a lasting ceasefire — or better yet, peace agreement — it will take a few months for normal levels of jet fuel production and delivery to resume,” airline industry analyst Henry Harteveldt, president of Atmosphere Research Group, said.

Iran's reversal of its decision to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and President Donald Trump's insistence on maintaining a U.S. blockade of Iranian ports illustrated the shakiness of prospects for oil flowing reliably again from the Persian Gulf and with it, an easing of the price pressure on airlines and their customers.

“My advice to travelers is this: If you find a flight whose schedule fits yours, with a fare you can afford, and on an airline you can at least tolerate, book it,” Harteveldt said. “But — and I cannot emphasize this enough —do not book a Basic Economy fare,” the cheapest but also the most restrictive airline ticket class.

Along with charging for checked bags and seat selection, most North American airlines do not give refunds or travel credits to passengers with Basic Economy tickets if they don't cancel their trips within 24 hours of purchase. Policies may vary, but spending more for a Standard Economy ticket provides more flexibility, according to Harteveldt.

open image in gallery Airlines have announced flight cuts in the US in response to a jet fuel crisis brought on by the Iran war ( Getty )

Paying more up-front for a refundable ticket also prove advantageous because “if the prices start to dramatically change, you can cancel and rebook for the better price,” Gilad said.

Travel experts say that for now, longstanding booking guidance offers a baseline for how early to reserve a flight to get the lowest airfare: international flights are typically the cheapest about two to five months in advance, and domestic trips about three to six weeks out.

Last-minute bookings and other situations that typically command higher prices are likely to keep climbing, Gilad said.

“Remember, especially if you’re traveling on the major airlines, they’re going to have more ability to adjust fares. If you book too close to your travel date, you’re going to pay more," he said. "The farther out you can book, the better.”

Keep an open mind

Travelers who don't want or need to reach a specific place at a specific time can find it easier to save on airfare. Shifting departure or return dates by a day or two — especially from peak weekends and holidays to midweek — often yields big price differences.

Choosing a different destination also may pay off. A flight from the U.S. may be significantly cheaper to one European city than another. Since budget airlines and trains connect much of Europe, and trains, an airport it cost less to get to can still provide easy access to a lot of other places.

Consumers not set on a certain arrival destination can try tools like Skyscanner’s “Explore Everywhere” feature to look for less-expensive options.

Looking beyond the closest airport for departures also can make a meaningful difference. Major hubs tend to offer more flights and lower fares than smaller regional airports.

In some cases, booking a separate short flight or train to a hub will unlock a cheaper long-haul airfare — think Milwaukee versus Chicago’s O’Hare International Airport.

Travel light

Sticking to a carry-on bag, when possible, can help avoid the higher fees for checking luggage that many major U.S. airlines introduced recently, including Delta, American, United, Southwest and JetBlue.

If packing light is not an option, plan ahead because airlines typically charge more to add bags closer to departure, especially within 24 hours of a flight.

Redeem your points

While fares are going up, the number of airline points needed for many flights has not increased at the same pace, said Adam Morvitz, CEO of points.me, a loyalty rewards redemption search platform.

Airlines still need to fill seats, Morvitz said, and offering more of them for fewer points is one way to do it.

Customers without enough frequent-flyer miles or credit card points for a round-trip ticket still can redeem their travel rewards for one leg of a journey and free up cash for other travel expenses.

Many travelers redeem points directly through their credit card’s booking portal, where they’re typically worth about 1 cent each, Morvitz said. Transferring points to airline loyalty programs often unlocks significantly better value because most major credit card issuers partner with a range of airlines.

Take American Express, whose points can be transferred to Air France’s Flying Blue program. Travelers who don’t want to book with Air France still can use those points with the airline's partner carriers, such as Delta, Morvitz said.

“Points are a form of wealth, and consumers should recognize that those points increase spending power," he said.

Explore travel credit cards

For those new to travel credit cards, sign-up bonuses may yield benefits that can be put to use as soon as this summer. Some bonuses are large enough to cover a flight after meeting a minimum spending requirement.

"Even if you were to travel the entire year, taking one trip per month, you would still earn more points simply by signing up for the card than actually sitting on a seat and flying,” Morvitz said.

Points and rewards can add up through everyday spending on groceries, dining and gas. Some cards include perks like free or discounted checked bags.

A British widow, 69, died in a road crash in Ghana, having lost an estimated £1 million to a series of online romance frauds, an inquest has heard.

Janet Fordham, 69, suffered fatal injuries in the collision on 14 February 2023, after travelling to the country the previous October.

Devon Coroner’s Court heard Mrs Fordham had fallen victim to several online scams over a five-year period, which saw her lose her home and life savings – estimated to be up to £1 million.

At the time of travelling to Ghana, the retired housekeeper was living in a caravan at the home of her son Martin and daughter-in-law Melanie Fordham in Honiton, Devon.

Mrs Fordham began using online dating websites in 2017 and met a man claiming to be a British Army sergeant major working in Syria, who needed her help to get gold bars to the UK.

“He was retiring soon to return to the UK. She said they were in love and they were going to buy a house together,” Mrs Fordham said.

“Janet mentioned nothing about any money at that point, but I remember candidly saying to her that it all seemed a little unbelievable, and the next thing he would be asking for money.

“I told her categorically not to send him any. Janet had been sending money to him, but we didn’t find out about this until years later. I believe she gave him around £150,000.”

Mrs Fordham later learned she had been further defrauded by a “diplomat” after her UK bank accounts were frozen.

“I think she realised that she had been scammed, but initially struggled to accept it,” Mrs Fordham said.

“We’re not clear how Janet transitioned from one fraud to the next.

“We became aware that she transferred money by several means, including bank transfers, wire transfers at the post office, and potentially a travel agent.

“The banks, post office etc stopped her from using their services, transferring money, because they recognised that it was fraud.”

The inquest heard that another man, named as Kofi, contacted Mrs Fordham saying he was a doctor in Ghana working part-time in a friend’s mobile phone repair shop.

“He was working on a phone that saw messages to and from Janet on there. He believed Janet had been scammed,” Mrs Fordham said.

“He felt compelled to help her get her money back. So, he took her phone number and made contact.”

Police spoke with Mrs Fordham about Kofi, but officers could not further the investigation due to her lack of engagement.

The court heard Mrs Fordham contacted police again because her mother-in-law was continuing to transfer money abroad using bitcoin and ATMs.

“Whether she was in so deep, she couldn’t accept it was all gone, she had to keep piling money in the hope of getting something back,” she said.

“Whether she genuinely believed what she was being told, we will never know.”

She also borrowed money from other family members, which totalled around £140,000, and was also in arrears on loans and credit cards.

“Janet wouldn’t tell us much, so we started opening some of her mail and discovered that she had cashed in a chunk of her pension,” Mrs Fordham said.

“She was withdrawing the maximum £500 a day, we believe to stockpile, and then transferred cash as the banks had stopped her doing electronic transfers.

“I was very aware that we don’t know everything and there is probably a whole lot more.”

In October 2022, Mrs Fordham flew to Ghana to meet Kofi who she was romantically linked to.

“As a family, we tried everything to stop her, but she was adamant,” Mrs Fordham said.

“I spoke to her doctor, sought legal advice, but because she was of sound mind, albeit brainwashed, she was deemed to have capacity and there was nothing we could do.”

Detective Sergeant Ben Smith, of Devon and Cornwall Police, said officers had contact with Mrs Fordham about allegations of fraud in 2017, 2020 and 2022.

“It shows Janet Fordham as a sustained victim of fraud throughout that period,” he said.

“It’s believed that Janet has sent a considerable amount of money, estimated at between £800,000 and £1 million over that period.

“As a result, she had used all her savings, sold her home and land, and was living in a caravan with Martin and Melanie in their garden.

“Police throughout these investigations have endeavoured to do everything they can to persuade Janet not to have any contact with the criminals and not to hand over money.

“There was no issue with capacity and that she was making these decisions of her own free will.”

Det Sgt Smith said on the day she died Mrs Fordham and Kofi were driving from Accra to the Oti region “to get approval from a family member for marriage”.

Kofi was driving when the car left the road and crashed, with Mrs Fordham suffering fatal injuries.

He later pleaded guilty to driving offences and received a suspended prison sentence and fine, the court heard.

Det Sgt Smith confirmed there was no evidence of any third-party involvement in Mrs Fordham’s death.

The inquest continues.
